AMZN.rationale: Amazon presents a solid fundamental case with strong trajectory. Q3 2025 showed $180.2B revenue with accelerating EPS growth (Q1: $1.59 → Q2: $1.68 → Q3: $1.95), robust operating cash flow ($35.5B quarterly), and a fortress balance sheet ($369.6B equity, $55.1B debt, debt-to-equity 0.149). AWS is the profit engine, generating ~57-59% of operating income on ~18-21% of revenue, with Q1 2026 growth accelerating to 28% YoY. The business model is structurally sound: retail drives scale and customer acquisition while AWS, advertising (~$68.5B annualized), and subscriptions generate the profits. However, several factors temper the score. Valuation is mid-range vs own history: P/E of 34.7 sits within the 28-39 range of the past year, not cheap. The massive $200B 2026 capex plan for AI infrastructure is compressing free cash flow (FCF fell to $11.2B in FY2025 despite $139.5B operating cash flow), and Goldman Sachs warns this spending could erode ROE by ~700bps. Regulatory headwinds are material: FTC antitrust trial scheduled for October 2026, EU cloud procurement review, and a $2.5B Prime settlement already paid. Competition is intensifying from Azure (40% growth) and Google Cloud (63% growth) outpacing AWS. The near-term catalyst is Prime Day (June 23-26) and Q2 earnings on July 30, with consensus expecting 16.8% revenue growth and 8.3% EPS growth. News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.354 over 90 days). The stock is 12% below its 52-week high of $278.56, having recovered +17.1% from the March trough. Overall, a quality franchise with strong growth vectors but not undervalued enough to warrant a higher score given capex pressure and regulatory risk.
